direct_claims: This chart reports the share of the population living on less than $30 a day across world regions and selected countries.
The title identifies the subject as poverty measured by a $30-a-day threshold.
The source is Our World in Data using World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform data.
The values are intended to be comparable across countries because the data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.
In this dataset, a person is counted as in poverty if they live on less than the equivalent of $30 per day, using an international-dollar concept rather than simple market exchange rates.
The note says the data is expressed in international-$ at 2021 prices.
The note also says that, depending on the country and year, the measure may refer either to income after taxes and benefits or to consumption per capita.
Because the table is truncated, any statement about the full global ranking of all countries would be incomplete.
